summary: Master Early Warning Systems (EWS) and disaster monitoring. Learn Sendai Framework, GIS mapping, and CAP protocols to enhance community resilience.
lede: Early warning systems connect hazard monitoring, forecasting and communication so people at risk can act before disasters cause harm. This course is for disaster risk, forecasting, emergency response, mapping and resilience professionals who need to turn environmental data into timely action. It covers multi-hazard risk mapping, sensor-network design, impact-based forecasting and alert protocols, with exercises in creating operational plans and messages.
audienceIntro: This intermediate-level program is tailored for professionals responsible for the design, implementation, and management of disaster resilience and emergency communication frameworks.
modules: Foundations of Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems
Risk Knowledge and Spatial Hazard Mapping
prerequisites: Participants should have at least two years of experience in disaster risk management, emergency services, environmental monitoring, or urban planning. Basic familiarity with GIS concepts and data management is recommended. No prior programming or coding knowledge is required for this course.
